key_insight: This baseline natural history study establishes the first large U.S. CADASIL cohort and shows that genetically defined NOTCH3 carriers can be systematically characterized with clinical, cognitive, MRI, and biomarker measures to support VCID research.
clinical_relevance: CADASIL offers a single-cause model of small vessel disease that may help identify biomarkers and outcome measures relevant to vascular cognitive impairment and dementia.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
Adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants underwent standardized clinical, cognitive, physical, MRI, genetics, and proteomics assessments.
Central genetic review grouped pathogenic/likely pathogenic NOTCH3 variants into low-, medium-, or high-risk tiers.
evidence_signal: The baseline analytic cohort included 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, with group comparisons and multivariable adjustment used to assess differences.
watch_item: Findings are baseline and cross-sectional, so they cannot establish progression, causal effects, or broad generalizability beyond this relatively homogeneous cohort.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
